# edubba-cuneiform-101 — one card per sign taught in the course, generated by
# bin/deck_export.rb from the Edubba registries and Sign Codex.
# Import into Anki (File > Import), then enable FSRS in the deck
# options for evidence-backed scheduling.
𒀸	<b>one</b> · AŠ · <i>[aš]</i> · one; single<br>One stroke. The first mark any scribe ever pressed into clay, and the first sign you learned to write. If you can make one wedge, you already own it — there is nothing else to hold.<br><i>1(aš) lu₂ šu ba-ti</i> — "one (unit) — the man received (it)" (urn:nabu:cdli:p010721:obverse:1:3, license: attribution)<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒁹	<b>tally</b> · DIŠ · <i>[diš]</i> · one (counting); item marker<br>A tally mark, standing upright like the person it counts. Every culture that ever counted on a doorpost or a prison wall drew exactly this stroke; the scribes simply pressed theirs into clay. One stands, one is counted.<br><i>5(diš) še</i> — "five (units) of barley" (urn:nabu:cdli:p010519:obverse:1:4, license: attribution)<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒌋	<b>ten</b> · U · <i>[u]</i> · ten<br>Ten is a corner: when your tallies reach ten, you stop drawing strokes and stamp a corner instead — the counting hand folding a full set into one dent. Tallies stand in rows; tens sit as hooks.<br><i>1(u) še gur lugal</i> — "ten gur of barley, by the royal gur" (urn:nabu:cdli:p100077:obverse:1, license: attribution)<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒀀	<b>water</b> · A · <i>[a]</i> · water<br>Water runs in two thin channels, side by side — two long wedges like irrigation ditches seen from the air. Everything in Sumer begins with water in a channel; so does the sign list.<br><i>a mu-na-ru</i> — "dedicated this to him" (urn:nabu:cdli:p216758, license: attribution)<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒆳	<b>mountain</b> · KUR · <i>[kur]</i> · mountain; foreign land<br>A mountain range needs three peaks — count the wedges: one, two, three, a child's drawing of a skyline. Where the flat land ends, the kur begins.<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒀭	<b>heaven</b> · AN · <i>[an], diŋir</i> · heaven; god (determinative {d})<br>Heaven is where the stars are: one star stands for all of it — and for everyone who lives there. Whenever you see the star, look up: sky, sky-god, or any god at all.<br><i>diŋir-diŋir</i> — "god-god" — the star doubled, on an Early Dynastic roster (a name or divine pair; approximate) (urn:nabu:cdli:p010019:reverse:4:2', license: attribution)<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒌓	<b>day</b> · UD · <i>[ud], utu</i> · day; sun<br>Day breaks where the sun clears the ridge — a big wedge of light pushing over the horizon line. When the texts want "on that day," "in those days," "daylight," this is the sign that rises.<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒊺	<b>barley</b> · ŠE · <i>[še]</i> · barley; grain<br>Barley hangs heavy: a stalk with kernels stacked up both sides, drawn the way a farmer would draw it. Wherever wealth is being counted, look for the little ear of grain.<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒆠	<b>place</b> · KI · <i>[ki]</i> · earth; place (determinative {ki})<br>A place on a map: a plot of ground marked out with its boundary lines drawn through it — a surveyor's diamond. Where the star means the world above, this fenced plot means the ground you stand on.<br><i>ki-en-gi</i> — Kiengi — Sumer, in its own oldest name (urn:nabu:cdli:p010447:reverse:2:6, license: attribution)<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒃲	<b>big</b> · GAL · <i>[gal]</i> · big, great<br>Big things get the big open wedges: the sign spreads wide like arms flung out to show this big. Whatever stands next to it — house, man, mountain — has just been enlarged.<br><i>lugal-gal-zu</i> — "The king knows greatness" (approximate) (urn:nabu:cdli:p010064:reverse:3:6, license: attribution)<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒈬	<b>name</b> · MU · <i>[mu]</i> · name; year<br>Your name, written down, is what survives of you — and in Sumer, each year's name was the one deed that survived of it. One sign for both: what a thing is called is what it was.<br><i>lu₂-diŋir-mu</i> — Lu-diŋirmu — "my man of the god" (approximate) (urn:nabu:cdli:p010063:obverse:7:11, license: attribution)<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒂍	<b>house</b> · É · <i>[e]</i> · house, temple<br>A house in cross-section: tall frame, floors barred across, one of the most wedge-heavy signs you own — because a house takes work to build. If a word starts with this sign, someone lives or worships inside it.<br><i>e₂ ku₃</i> — "the pure house" — a temple's stock epithet (urn:nabu:cdli:p010644:obverse:3:2, license: attribution)<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒁾	<b>tablet</b> · DUB · <i>[dub]</i> · (clay) tablet<br>A tablet with its ruling still visible: a slab crossed by the lines a scribe pressed to keep the writing straight. The script's own self-portrait — the thing you are reading, drawn inside itself.<br><i>dub-sar</i> — "scribe" — tablet-writer, plainly (urn:nabu:cdli:p010009:reverse:1:2, license: attribution)<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒈗	<b>king</b> · LUGAL · <i>[lugal]</i> · king<br>The king is the big man — the sign says so out loud. It is also one of the heaviest signs you own, about a dozen wedges: royalty takes work to write, which is easy to believe.<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒇽	<b>man</b> · LU2 · <i>[lu]</i> · man, person<br>A man standing at his plot: the wedges square off a little frame — one person's standing room. Every proverb's "a man…," every roster's "person who…" begins here; add big and he becomes the king.<br><i>lu₂ šu ba-ti</i> — "the man received (it)" (urn:nabu:cdli:p010490:obverse:4:2', license: attribution)<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒌉	<b>child</b> · TUR · <i>[dumu], tur</i> · child, son (dumu); small (tur)<br>The child is the small one of the house — the sign is compact, few wedges, small on purpose. When a name needs a father, this little sign does the introducing: son of.<br><i>dumu-zi</i> — Dumuzi, "the true son" (approximate) (urn:nabu:cdli:p010019:reverse:3:3', license: attribution)<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒂗	<b>lord</b> · EN · <i>[en]</i> · lord; high priest<br>The lord holds the middle of the sign like a seat — a frame with the bar of authority across it. Where prayers and epics need a superior — god, king, master — this sign opens the address.<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒆤	<b>spirit</b> · KID · <i>[lil], kid</i> · air, spirit (lil₂) — the LIL of Enlil<br>A woven mat is mostly spirit: air held in a lattice of reeds. Wind you cannot draw — but you can draw the thing it passes through. One humble mat, and it writes the name of the king of the gods.<br><i>išib an-na-ke₄</i> — "purification priest of An" (urn:nabu:cdli:p216758, license: attribution)<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒈾	<b>stone</b> · NA · <i>[na]</i> · [na]; stone in some words<br>A stone is what you find everywhere and build with anywhere — this sign is the script's fieldstone, mortared into names, nouns, and verb chains alike. Small, hard, indispensable.<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒉌	<b>oil</b> · NI · <i>[ni], i₃</i> · [ni]; oil, butter as i₃<br>An oil jar tips forward, ready to pour. Oil slicks into everything — food, lamps, offerings, and half the verb chains you will read, where the jar quietly primes the verb.<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒅎	<b>storm</b> · IM · <i>[im]</i> · clay; rain, storm<br>A storm front: one long wedge of cloud with the slanting strokes of rain driving off it. What the storm leaves behind is mud — and mud, in Sumer, is what you write on.<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒄥	<b>bushel</b> · GUR · <i>[gur]</i> · gur — the great capacity measure of grain accounts<br>The bushel basket at the granary door: everything pours through it, nothing is official until it has. In an account line it stands at the end like the stamp on a receipt — …by the bushel.<br><i>1(u) še gur lugal</i> — "ten gur of barley, by the royal gur" (urn:nabu:cdli:p100077:obverse:1, license: attribution)<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒊕	<b>head</b> · SAG · <i>[saŋ]</i> · head; first<br>A head in profile, tipped back: forehead, jaw, the neck-line under it. Whatever is saŋ comes first — the head of a line, the head of a household, the front of anything.<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒅗	<b>mouth</b> · KA · <i>[ka]</i> · mouth<br>A head, but look at the mouth: the hatching sits right where the lips are, like a speech-bubble scribbled onto a face. Feed it water and it drinks; feed it a portion and it eats.<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒅘	<b>drink</b> · KA×A · <i>[naŋ]</i> · to drink<br>Drink: a mouth with water already in it. The script does not describe the act — it stages it, one sign swallowed by another. Once you have seen the little streams inside the jaw, you cannot unsee the gulp.<br><i>ga-naŋ-naŋ</i> — "Milk, drink, drink" (approximate) (urn:nabu:cdli:p010652, license: attribution)<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
𒅥	<b>eat</b> · KA×GAR · <i>[gu]</i> · to eat<br>Eat: the mouth with its portion already in. Same staging as its twin drink — only the filling differs: streams of water to drink, a packed ration to eat. Check what is in the mouth before you read it.<br><i>ga-gu₇-gu₇</i> — "Milk, eat, eat" (approximate) (urn:nabu:cdli:p010652, license: attribution)<br>Edubba · edubba.ac · CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted lines carry their own licenses	edubba edubba-cuneiform-101
